name: 北海道名物らー麺 えびそば 一幻 新宿店 (Hokkaido Meibutsu Ramen Ebisoba Ichigen Shin)

claims.text: Broth, tare (shoyu/miso/shio), and noodles are all wheat/gluten-containing standard ramen components; no gluten-free process identified.
The shoyu ramen's noodles, soup, and ebi-ten topping all contain wheat, per the retail product's allergen listing for the same recipe line.
Broth is pork-fat/pork-bone and shrimp based; no vegetarian or vegan broth option identified.

Chef Arai works Japanese fermented soy products — soy-sauce moromi and kuromame (black bean) miso — into his French dishes as a seasoning base, which typically means wheat-containing soy products are present in multiple courses of the tasting menu.
Because the dinner course is entirely omakase, the restaurant asks guests in advance about allergies and disliked ingredients so the multi-course menu can be tailored before each visit.
HOMMAGE holds two stars in the Michelin Guide, recognized for delicate French cooking that folds in Japanese ingredients and umami depth rooted in the chef's Asakusa upbringing.

name: 自家製麺NO11 ASAKUSA (Jikaseimen NO11 Asakusa)

claims.text: The broth is a shoyu (soy sauce) based, emulsified pork-bone soup; no wheat-free soy sauce, tamari, or gluten-free broth alternative is described in any source.

All broth is pork-bone based and every bowl comes with pork toppings by default; no vegetarian or vegan broth or topping substitution appears in the menu as described by reviewers (Ramen: ¥1,200, Pork Ramen: ¥1,600).

name: 十割蕎麦 嵯峨谷 渋谷東急本店前店 (Juwari Soba Sagatani – Shibuya Tokyu Honten-)

claims.text: Tempura and kakiage (fried in wheat-flour batter) are regular menu items alongside the soba, and no dedicated gluten-free fryer has been confirmed for this location.
The tsuyu is a soy-sauce-and-mirin kaeshi over a concentrated bonito dashi ('だしよく、甘め濃いめのきりっとした...カエシ'); standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, and no wheat-free tsuyu has been confirmed.
The soba tsuyu is dashi-based with bonito rather than a kombu-only broth, so the standard bowl is not vegan; no plant-based dashi alternative was found in available menu information.
The soba itself is 十割 (100% buckwheat) with no wheat flour or mountain-yam binder added — a genuinely wheat-free noodle, which is unusual for such an affordable chain.

name: 十割蕎麦 さがたに 新宿京王モール店（嵯峨谷） (Juwari Soba Sagatani — Shinjuku Keio Mall)

claims.text: Restaurants in most cases boil udon and soba in the same large pot (same water), so cross-contamination via the boiling water requires caution; and restaurant menus have no obligation to display allergens.

Many restaurants share frying oil for tempura, tonkatsu and other fried foods; Sagatani's tempura is described by a user as low-quality (soba is the flagship, tempura is cost-cut) — indicating no dedicated GF frying setup.

GF blog promoting Sagatani frames it as gluten-free for people doing GF 'for daily performance and health,' and notes tempura/tempura flakes contain gluten and regular soy sauce is brewed with wheat — i.e., strict-GF diners should avoid those — which is lifestyle-GF framing, not a celiac-safety guarantee.

Search-surfaced FindMeGlutenFree text ('ask for gluten free menu... they change the flour to rice for frying... gluten-free soy sauce available') does not clearly attribute these accommodations to the Shinjuku Keio Mall branch and appears conflated across Sagatani/Shibuya locations; unverifiable and single-source.

Standard Japanese soy sauce (shoyu), the base of soba tsuyu, is typically brewed from wheat and soybeans together — this is general Japanese food-labeling guidance, not a statement specific to this shop's own recipe, but it applies to conventional tsuyu of the kind this chain serves.
The chain's broth is described as made with kombu and a blend of dried bonito (katsuobushi) stocks for both the cold and hot tsuyu, meaning the soup base is fish-derived and not vegan.
Noodles are 100% buckwheat (juwari) with no wheat used as a binder, milled fresh in-store daily on an electric stone mill — a genuine plus versus ordinary soba, which typically blends in wheat flour.

name: かめや 新宿店 (Kameya Shinjuku-ten (Kameya Shinjuku))

claims.text: Standing (tachigui) soba shops like this one typically raise the wheat-flour ratio in their noodles so the strands hold up to fast prep and handling — the soba here is not a low-gluten or gluten-free product.
The signature dishes are served in a deliberately concentrated, dark soy-sauce-based soba tsuyu (dipping/soup broth), the shop's defining house style.
The signature ten-tama soba is topped with a soft hot-spring egg (onsen tamago) and kakiage tempura over a non-vegan tsuyu broth.

Menu listings show a みたらし (mitarashi) shiratama flavor whose sauce ingredients are 本醸造醤油・本みりん・きび糖・国産葛粉 — i.e., brewed soy sauce (wheat-containing in standard Japanese honjozo shoyu), refuting the current GF rationale that no soy sauce/wheat appears on this menu.
白玉手箱 and dango flavor lineup explicitly includes みたらし (mitarashi) alongside あんこ/ずんだ/抹茶 — confirming the soy-sauce flavor is a core, regularly-prepared menu item, not a rare seasonal add-on.
Menu itemization corroborating the mitarashi soy-sauce flavor and shared shiratama toppings across kakigori/anmitsu.

Reference confirming 黒蜜 (kuromitsu) is produced from sugarcane (boiled cane juice / brown sugar), not honey — so the 'homemade syrup (honey)' phrasing in one English auto-translation is a mistranslation of みつ and does NOT indicate a vegan-disqualifying honey ingredient in the core syrups.

Menu is dessert-focused (rice-flour dumplings, sugar syrups, agar jelly) with no soy sauce or dashi-based savory items described, reducing the most common hidden-wheat/hidden-fish risks found in Japanese savory dishes.

name: 甘味処 西山（旧店名：西山菓子店） (Kanmidokoro Nishiyama (formerly Nishiyama Ka)

claims.text: The famous 'Fukufuku manju' is made fresh and steamed on demand, using simple ingredients: wheat, sugar, and anko... They prepare items as much as possible in-house at their shop. — confirms daily raw-wheat-flour handling in the same premises as the anmitsu/kakigori/shiratama.
福々まんじゅうの原料は膨張剤以外は保存料などの添加物を一切使用せず、小麦と砂糖とあんだけのシンプルなもので作っています — signature bun is wheat-based and housemade.
Search returned no gluten-free/allergen/celiac information for 甘味処 西山; recommendation is to contact the shop directly — no shop-issued GF accommodation exists.
No celiac or gluten-free review of Nishiyama found on FindMeGlutenFree (Taito City) or HappyCow; the shop is absent from coeliac Tokyo guides' safe lists.
Handcrafted shiratama and two scoops of housemade ice cream in the Nishiyama anmitsu — dairy ice cream confirmed on the signature item (vegan concern).
Anko (red bean paste), ice cream, and other sweets are made in-house daily using carefully selected raw ingredients, per the shop's own long-stated approach to sourcing.
